slides.title: Severe Acute Malnutrition: WHO 10 Steps
slides.subtitle: Diagnosis, stabilisation, rehabilitation & discharge in one swipe

slides.title: Diagnosing SAM (6–59 months)
slides.subtitle: Any ONE of these is enough
points: **MUAC < 11.5 cm**
**Weight-for-height < −3 SD** (WHO growth standards)
**Bilateral pitting oedema** (nutritional oedema)
Admit (complicated SAM) if **oedema**, **failed appetite test** or a **medical complication**
Uncomplicated SAM with good appetite: **community care with RUTF**
slides.highlight: MUAC tape colours: red < 11.5 cm · yellow 11.5–12.5 cm · green ≥ 12.5 cm.

slides.title: Steps 1 & 2: Hypoglycaemia, Hypothermia
slides.subtitle: Treat both in the first hours
points: Hypoglycaemia = blood glucose **< 54 mg/dL (3 mmol/L)**
Give **50 mL of 10% glucose** or sucrose, orally or by NG tube
Unconscious: **10% dextrose 5 mL/kg IV**, then feeds by NG
Hypothermia = axillary **< 35 °C**: skin-to-skin with mother, cover head, warm room
Start feeds at once, **2-hourly, day and night**
slides.highlight: Hypoglycaemia and hypothermia usually occur together and suggest serious infection.

slides.title: Step 3: Dehydration
slides.subtitle: ReSoMal, not standard ORS
points: ReSoMal has **less sodium (45)** and **more potassium (40 mmol/L)**
**5 mL/kg every 30 min for 2 h**, orally or by NG
Then **5–10 mL/kg/h** for up to 10 h, alternating hours with F-75
Stop if **pulse and respiratory rate rise**: sign of fluid overload
**No IV fluids** unless in shock: **15 mL/kg over 1 h**, then reassess
slides.highlight: Signs of dehydration are unreliable in SAM: sunken eyes and skin pinch can mislead.

slides.title: Steps 4, 5 & 6
slides.subtitle: Electrolytes · Infection · Micronutrients
points: Extra **potassium 3–4 mmol/kg/day** and **magnesium 0.4–0.6 mmol/kg/day**
**No diuretics** for oedema
**Antibiotics for every child**: amoxicillin if well, **ampicillin + gentamicin** if complicated
**Vitamin A, folic acid, zinc, copper** from day 1
**No iron** in stabilisation: start only when gaining weight
slides.highlight: Iron in the first week can worsen infection and oxidative damage: classic exam trap.

slides.title: Step 7: Cautious Feeding (F-75)
slides.subtitle: Starts on day 1
points: F-75 = **75 kcal per 100 mL**, low protein
**130 mL/kg/day** (**100 mL/kg/day** if severe oedema)
Feeds **2-hourly → 3-hourly → 4-hourly** as the child settles
Switch to **F-100** when appetite returns and oedema is reducing (often within a week)
Transition: same volume for 2 days, then **+10 mL per feed** until some is left over
slides.highlight: Too much too soon risks refeeding syndrome and heart failure.

slides.title: Step 8: Catch-up Growth
slides.subtitle: Rehabilitation phase, weeks 2–6
points: **150–220 kcal/kg/day**, protein **4–6 g/kg/day**
**Start iron** now
Weigh daily: weight gain **> 10 g/kg/day = good**
**5–10 = moderate**, **< 5 = poor**: look for infection or feeding problems
slides.highlight: Steps 1–7 belong to week 1 (stabilisation); steps 8–10 to weeks 2–6.

slides.title: Steps 9 & 10 + Discharge
slides.subtitle: Care, follow-up and when to send home
points: Step 9: **sensory stimulation & emotional support**, mother involved in play
Step 10: teach **energy-dense home feeding**, complete vaccines, plan follow-up
Discharge: **MUAC ≥ 12.5 cm** or **WHZ ≥ −2 SD**
AND **no oedema for at least 2 weeks**
slides.highlight: Mnemonic for the 'No's in SAM: no IV, no diuretics, no early iron.

caption:
Severe acute malnutrition: the WHO 10 steps, from admission to discharge 🥣

📏 SAM (6–59 mo), any one: MUAC < 11.5 cm · WHZ < −3 SD · bilateral pitting oedema

🩸 1–2: Hypoglycaemia (< 54 mg/dL → 50 mL 10% glucose; unconscious 10% dextrose 5 mL/kg IV) & hypothermia (< 35 °C → skin-to-skin, warm)
💧 3: ReSoMal 5 mL/kg every 30 min × 2 h, then 5–10 mL/kg/h. No IV unless shock (15 mL/kg over 1 h)
💊 4–6: K 3–4 & Mg 0.4–0.6 mmol/kg/day · antibiotics for all · vitamin A, folate, zinc, copper · no iron yet
🍼 7: F-75, 130 mL/kg/day, 2 → 3 → 4-hourly
📈 8: F-100/RUTF 150–220 kcal/kg/day, start iron, target gain > 10 g/kg/day
🏠 9–10: play & care, follow-up plan
✅ Discharge: MUAC ≥ 12.5 cm or WHZ ≥ −2 SD, no oedema for 2 weeks
